content:
Here’s a concise summary:

When analyzing algorithms, the time taken depends on the input size (e.g., sorting 6 elements vs. 6 billion). Instead of fixed numbers, we express running time as a function of input size to understand its behavior. Typically, we focus on **upper bounds** (worst-case guarantees) because they provide users with reliable limits (e.g., "this won’t take more than 3 seconds"), ensuring predictability—unlike lower bounds, which offer no meaningful assurance.
